full_judgment:
2. Facts of the case, in brief, are that the respondent as plaintiff instituted Small Causes Court Suit No. 4 of 2000 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, and S.C.C. Judge, Kushtia Sadar, seeking eviction of the defendant from the suit premises classifying him as a habitual defaulter in paying monthly rent at the rate of Tk. 345/- per month from January 1995 till filing of the suit on 04.06.2000. A notice under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act was sent on 07.03.2000. After sending that notice the relationship between the landlord and the tenant was terminated. 

 3. The defendant-petitioner contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material statements made in the plaint contending, inter alia, that he was in the habit of paying rent regularly, but the plaintiff suddenly enhanced rent twice and, thereafter, the defendant started depositing rent with the rent Controller through Miscellaneous Case No. 22 of 1995 and as such he was not a defaulter. Thereafter, the defendant sent rent with increased 10% to the plaintiff. The defendant did not receive any notice from the plaintiff. The relationship between the landlord and tenant has not been terminated. The defendant claims that the plaintiff will transfer the possession of the property to another, and that is why he filed the suit for eviction. Hence, the defendant prayed for dismissal of the suit. 

 9. The learned Judge of the Small Caused Court observed that in Miscellaneous Case No. 22 of 1995, which was filed by the defendant-petitioner, he did not submit any evidence of having deposited any money in respect of rent for the month of December 1997 and October 2002. Accordingly, the learned Judge of the S.C.C. Court found the petitioner to be a defaulter.
